title: ARSIA Onboarding Decision Payload
description: Payload structure for the onboarding decision message (intent: approval_decision) emitted by the onboarding gateway after completing the six-phase onboarding evaluation. The decision is either 'approved' (with token, capabilities, conformance result, and provenance) or 'denied' (with denial_reason, no token). Defined in ARSIA-Identity.md §7.6. Conformance check structure from §7.3. Provenance structure from §7.5. Capability scoping from §7.4.

type.description: Payload type identifier for the onboarding decision. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.6.

result.description: Decision result object. Structure varies based on the 'decision' value: 'approved' includes token, capability lists, conformance result, and provenance; 'denied' includes denial_reason and MUST NOT include token. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.6.

decision.description: The onboarding decision. 'approved': agent passes all phases and receives a scoped access token. 'denied': agent fails one or more phases. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.6.

effective_capabilities.description: Union of freely_allowed and oversight_required capabilities granted to the agent. Computed as (agent_declared ∩ policy_allowed) ∪ (agent_declared ∩ policy_oversight_required). Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.4 and §7.6.

freely_allowed.description: Capabilities the agent may invoke without additional oversight during the operational phase. Subset of effective_capabilities with policy status 'allowed'. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.4.

oversight_required.description: Capabilities the agent may invoke but each invocation MUST trigger a pending_approval flow (ARSIA-Actions.md §3.2) before execution. Subset of effective_capabilities with policy status 'oversight_required'. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.4.

token.description: JWT access token whose scope claim includes exactly the effective_capabilities. The token's sub claim MUST be the external agent's agent-id, iss claim MUST be the gateway's agent-id, exp claim MUST be set per policy.token_lifetime_seconds. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.6 and §9.1.

allOf.description: Token expiry time in RFC 3339 format with millisecond precision, UTC. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.6.

conformance_result.description: Aggregate result of the five Phase 2 conformance checks. REQUIRED for approval; SHOULD be included for denial to provide feedback. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.3 and §7.6.

provenance.description: Temporal provenance evidence recorded during Phase 4. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.5.

policy_version.description: Version identifier of the CapabilityPolicy applied during Phase 3. Establishes which policy version was in effect at onboarding time. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §8.1.

denial_reason.description: Reason for denial. 'discovery_failed': Phase 1 Step 1 failed (§7.2). 'identity_verification_failed': Phase 1 Steps 2-5 failed (§7.2). 'unacceptable_risk_classification': Phase 1 Step 6 — agent classified as unacceptable-risk (§7.2). 'conformance_failed': Phase 2 — one or more conformance checks failed (§7.3). 'no_permitted_capabilities': Phase 3 — no capabilities matched the policy (§8.3).

conformance-check.description: Result of a single conformance check run during Phase 2 of onboarding. Five normative checks are defined: CHECK-01 (envelope validity), CHECK-02 (signature verification), CHECK-03 (human oversight compliance), CHECK-04 (audit trail format), CHECK-05 (classification consistency). Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.3.

test_id.description: Identifier for the conformance check. Standard checks use CHECK-01 through CHECK-05. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.3.

status.description: Result status. 'pass': check criteria met. 'fail': check criteria not met. 'skip': preconditions not met (e.g. CHECK-05 skipped for non-high-risk agents, CHECK-04 skipped when audit endpoint unavailable). Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.3.

details.description: Human-readable details about the check result. Typically provided for 'fail' and 'skip' results to explain the outcome. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.3.

duration_ms.description: Duration of the check execution in milliseconds. May be omitted for skipped checks. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.3.

conformance-result.description: Aggregate result of the five conformance checks in Phase 2. ALL checks with status 'pass' or 'skip' MUST be achieved for Phase 2 to pass. If any check has status 'fail', Phase 2 fails. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.3.

checks.description: Array of individual conformance check results. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.3.

all_passed.description: true if every check has status 'pass' or 'skip'; false if any check has status 'fail'. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.3.

total_duration_ms.description: Total duration of all conformance checks in milliseconds. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.3.

provenance.description: Temporal provenance evidence of the external agent's existence and operational history, recorded during Phase 4. Provenance is informational — a false result SHOULD be logged as a warning but MUST NOT automatically deny onboarding. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.5.

allOf.description: The created_at field from the agent's IdentityRecord (ARSIA-Identity.md §1.2), establishing when the agent's identity was first created. RFC 3339 format with millisecond precision, UTC. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.5.

The processed_at timestamp of the earliest audit record from the agent's audit endpoint (/.well-known/arsia/audit), if available. Establishes earliest known operational activity. MUST NOT be earlier than identity_created_at. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.5.

provenance_verified.description: true if both identity_created_at and earliest_audit_record are present, are valid RFC 3339 timestamps, and earliest_audit_record is not earlier than identity_created_at. false otherwise. Per ARSIA-Identity.md §7.5.
